1.description: Brilliant red cardinals visiting feeders against fresh snow, males singing short whistles at dawn
1.childFriendlyNote: A bright red bird lands on the snowy feeder like a little Christmas ornament that can sing!

1.description: Chickadees flitting between feeders and branches, calling their buzzy "chick-a-dee-dee-dee"
1.childFriendlyNote: This tiny brave bird says its own name ("chicka-dee-dee-dee!") even when it's freezing cold

1.description: Rabbit tracks in fresh snow, paired hind prints ahead of smaller front prints in a bounding pattern
1.childFriendlyNote: Look for bunny tracks in the snow. Two big back feet land in front of two little front feet, like hopping exclamation marks!

1.description: Deer tracks and trails visible in snow, deer browsing on twigs and bark in woodland edges
1.childFriendlyNote: Heart-shaped hoof prints in the snow tell you a deer walked here. Follow the trail with your eyes!

1.description: Slate-grey juncos scratching on snowy ground beneath feeders, flashing white outer tail feathers
1.childFriendlyNote: These little grey "snowbirds" only visit in winter. Watch them flash white tail feathers when they fly away!

2.description: Cardinals at feeders in early morning, bright red against grey January skies
2.childFriendlyNote: A bright red bird lands on the snowy feeder like a little Christmas ornament that can sing!

2.description: Red-tailed hawks perched on bare trees or fence posts along snowy fields, hunting for mice
2.childFriendlyNote: A big hawk sits on a fence post like a statue, watching the snowy field for tiny mice scurrying below

2.description: Chickadees caching seeds in bark crevices, remembering hundreds of hiding spots
2.childFriendlyNote: This tiny brave bird says its own name ("chicka-dee-dee-dee!") even when it's freezing cold

2.description: Nuthatches creeping headfirst down tree trunks, probing bark for hibernating insects
2.childFriendlyNote: This funny bird walks down the tree trunk headfirst. No other bird does that! Listen for its nasal "yank yank" call

2.description: Fox tracks in snow: neat single-file prints, sometimes yellow urine marks on snow mounds
2.childFriendlyNote: Fox footprints walk in a perfect straight line in the snow, like a tightrope walker with furry paws!

3.description: Barred owls calling at dusk and dawn, "Who cooks for you? Who cooks for you-all?" Courtship season begins
3.childFriendlyNote: At bedtime, listen outside for an owl hooting "Who cooks for you? Who cooks for you-all?" It's looking for a sweetheart!

3.description: Cardinals beginning to sing more frequently at dawn, establishing territory even in deep winter
3.childFriendlyNote: The red cardinal whistles "Birdy birdy birdy!" from a bare branch. He's telling everyone this is his garden

3.description: Chickadees beginning their clear two-note "fee-bee" spring song on warmer mornings
3.childFriendlyNote: The chickadee has a new song! Instead of "chicka-dee" it whistles a sweet "fee-bee". Spring is on its mind

3.description: Downy woodpeckers drumming on resonant branches, the rapid tattoo carrying through bare winter woods
3.childFriendlyNote: A tiny woodpecker drums its beak super fast on a branch, rat-a-tat-tat! It's like a little drummer in the trees

3.description: Juncos foraging in flocks on snowy ground, scratching with both feet to uncover seeds
3.childFriendlyNote: Little grey snowbirds hop and scratch with both feet at once to find seeds hiding under the snow

4.description: Barred owls in full courtship, duetting calls echoing through bottomland woods at dusk
4.childFriendlyNote: Two owls call back and forth in the dark woods, "Who cooks for you?" "Who cooks for you!" They're falling in love!

4.description: Red-tailed hawks soaring over open fields on sunny days, scanning snowy ground for voles
4.childFriendlyNote: A huge hawk circles high above the snowy field without flapping. It rides invisible rivers of warm air!

4.description: Male cardinals singing loud clear whistles from prominent perches, day length increasing noticeably
4.childFriendlyNote: The cardinal sits on the tallest branch and sings as loud as he can. He wants the whole neighborhood to hear!

4.description: Nuthatches beginning courtship, male feeding female at feeders
4.childFriendlyNote: The boy nuthatch brings a seed to the girl nuthatch. Sharing food is how birds say "I like you!"

4.description: Rabbit tracks crisscrossing snowy yards, rabbits nibbling bark and twigs during lean winter months
4.childFriendlyNote: Bunnies have been nibbling the bark off little trees. You can see their tiny teeth marks if you look closely!

5.description: Barred owls nesting in large tree cavities, female on eggs while male hunts nearby
5.childFriendlyNote: The mama owl is sitting on her eggs in a big tree hole, keeping them warm while snow falls outside

5.description: Great horned owls already incubating eggs in old hawk or crow nests, deep hooting at dusk
5.childFriendlyNote: The biggest owl is already a mama! She sits on eggs in the snow, her fluffy feathers keeping babies warm like a blanket

5.description: Downy woodpeckers drumming more frequently, establishing nesting territories in bare woods
5.childFriendlyNote: The woodpecker picks the loudest branch to drum on, the louder the better to impress the lady woodpeckers!

5.description: Red-tailed hawks beginning aerial courtship displays, pairs circling together over nesting territory
5.childFriendlyNote: Two big hawks dance in the sky together, swooping and diving: it's their way of saying "let's be a family!"

5.description: Chickadees singing clear "fee-bee" whistles more often, pairs forming for the breeding season
5.childFriendlyNote: Chickadees are pairing up! A boy and girl chickadee stick together now, sharing seeds and singing "fee-bee"

5.description: Bald eagles gathering near open water on frozen rivers, fishing where ice has broken
5.childFriendlyNote: America's big eagle sits by a hole in the frozen river, waiting to grab a fish with its huge yellow feet!

6.description: Cardinals singing vigorously at dawn, days noticeably longer now
6.childFriendlyNote: The cardinal starts singing earlier every morning because the sun wakes up earlier too!

6.description: Great horned owl eggs hatching, fluffy white owlets in nests despite February cold
6.childFriendlyNote: Baby owls are hatching right now in the freezing cold! They're white fluffy puffballs with big dark eyes

6.description: Pairs of red-tails adding sticks to nest platforms in tall trees, courtship flights overhead
6.childFriendlyNote: The hawks are building a big stick nest way up high. They add new sticks to the same nest every year!

6.description: Downy woodpeckers excavating nest cavities in dead wood, wood chips falling below
6.childFriendlyNote: The woodpecker is drilling a round hole in a dead tree. It's building a bedroom! Look for wood chips on the ground

6.description: Deer yarding together in sheltered woods, conserving energy through deep snow
6.childFriendlyNote: Deer huddle together in the woods where the snow isn't so deep. They share paths to save energy, like friends sharing a sidewalk

7.description: Very first male red-winged blackbirds scouting marshy areas in southern Midwest, earliest harbinger of spring
7.childFriendlyNote: A black bird with red shoulders lands on a cattail and sings "conk-la-ree!". He's the first sign that spring is coming!

7.description: Barred owls vocal at dusk, calling loudly through bare woods during breeding season
7.childFriendlyNote: The owl calls "Who cooks for you?" through the cold dark woods. Listen just after sunset!

7.description: Cardinals singing strongly, pairs beginning to form, male feeding female
7.childFriendlyNote: The boy cardinal picks up a sunflower seed and gently puts it in the girl cardinal's beak, bird kisses!

7.description: Squirrels chasing each other through bare branches, mating season beginning
7.childFriendlyNote: Squirrels zoom through the bare trees chasing each other in wild spirals. They're playing a game of tag!

7.description: Chickadee pairs inspecting potential nest cavities in dead branches and old woodpecker holes
7.childFriendlyNote: Chickadee couples peek into little holes in trees. They're house-hunting for the perfect spot to raise babies!

8.description: Male red-winged blackbirds arriving in small groups, claiming cattail territories in wetlands
8.childFriendlyNote: Black birds with bright red shoulder patches sit on old cattails and sing "conk-la-ree!" Spring messengers!

8.description: Great horned owl nestlings growing rapidly, fuzzy white heads visible in stick nests
8.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy white baby owls peek over the edge of their big stick nest. They look like cotton balls with eyes!

8.description: Maple sap beginning to run on warm days when temperatures rise above freezing, freeze-thaw cycle pumping sap up
8.childFriendlyNote: When it freezes at night and warms up during the day, sweet water rises inside maple trees. People tap it to make syrup!

8.description: First small flocks of robins appearing in sheltered areas with remaining berries, not yet on lawns
8.childFriendlyNote: The first robins are back! They eat leftover berries from bushes. They'll move to the lawn when the ground thaws

8.description: Downy woodpeckers drumming on resonant branches, territorial pairs established
8.childFriendlyNote: The woodpecker finds the loudest branch to drum on (brrrrrr!) it's like a tiny jackhammer in the woods

9.description: Red-winged blackbirds now widespread in wetlands, males puffing red epaulets and singing from every cattail
9.childFriendlyNote: The blackbird puffs up his red shoulder patches like little flags and sings so loud. He wants everyone to know he's here!

9.description: Peak maple sugaring season, sap flowing freely during sunny days after cold nights
9.childFriendlyNote: Drip, drip, drip! Sweet maple sap drips into buckets hanging on trees. It takes 40 gallons of sap to make one gallon of syrup!

9.description: Robin flocks growing, some birds testing muddy patches on lawns for earthworms
9.childFriendlyNote: Robins hop across the yard tilting their heads sideways. They're listening for worms wiggling underground!

9.description: Skunk cabbage pushing through snow in wet woods and stream edges, generating its own heat to melt through
9.childFriendlyNote: This magical plant makes its own heat and melts through the snow! But don't sniff too close. It smells like a skunk!

9.description: First sandhill cranes arriving from the south, tall grey birds with red crowns in agricultural fields
9.childFriendlyNote: Tall grey birds with red caps stand in farm fields. Their rattling bugle call sounds like a dinosaur!

10.description: Sandhill cranes streaming through in large flocks, filling skies with rolling bugle calls during migration
10.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of huge grey birds fly over in V-shapes, making a rattling trumpet sound you can hear from far away!

10.description: Red-winged blackbirds in full chorus at every marsh, females now arriving to join territorial males
10.childFriendlyNote: The marsh is noisy! Every cattail has a blackbird on it, puffing his red patches and singing his heart out

10.description: Maple sugaring season continuing, buds swelling on branch tips signaling the end of the sap run
10.childFriendlyNote: The maple trees are getting ready to wake up. Their buds are swelling and soon the sweet sap will stop flowing

10.description: Skunk cabbage hoods fully emerged in wetlands, dark purple-streaked spathe curling around the spadix
10.childFriendlyNote: Strange purple hoods poke out of the swamp mud. They look like alien spaceships and smell like stinky socks!

10.description: Large robin flocks on thawing lawns, birds running and stopping to pull earthworms from soft ground
10.childFriendlyNote: Robins run-stop-run across the grass, then yank a wiggly worm right out of the ground, tug of war!

10.description: Woodcocks performing sky-dance courtship displays at dusk: buzzy "peent" calls followed by spiraling flights
10.childFriendlyNote: At sunset, a pudgy bird goes "peent!" then zooms way up into the sky twisting and twittering, what a show-off!

11.description: Peak crane migration, thousands gathering in staging areas on rivers and fields
11.childFriendlyNote: Thousands of cranes fill the fields and sky, their bugling calls so loud you have to shout to be heard!

11.description: Woodcock sky-dances at peak, males displaying every evening at dusk in wet meadow edges
11.childFriendlyNote: Every evening the funny round bird goes "peent!" then rockets into the sky, spiraling and twittering back down!

11.description: Red-winged blackbird territories fully established, males chasing rivals away from cattail stands
11.childFriendlyNote: The blackbird chases any bird that comes near his cattails. He guards them like a tiny fierce knight!

11.description: Killdeer returned to open fields and gravel lots, running and calling their loud "kill-deer" cry
11.childFriendlyNote: A brown bird screams "kill-deer! kill-deer!" as it runs across the parking lot. It likes to nest on gravel!

11.description: Silver maples blooming with tiny red-pink flowers before leaves emerge, one of the earliest native trees to flower
11.childFriendlyNote: Look up! Bare branches have fuzzy red flowers. The silver maple is the first tree to bloom, even before its leaves come out

11.description: First spring peepers calling from vernal pools on warm evenings, high-pitched sleigh-bell chorus
11.childFriendlyNote: Tiny frogs no bigger than your thumb make a huge noise. Hundreds peeping together sound like jingle bells in the pond!

12.description: Spring peepers in full chorus at ponds and wetlands, deafening wall of high-pitched peeping on warm evenings
12.childFriendlyNote: The pond is so loud with tiny frogs peeping that you can hear them from inside your house with the windows closed!

12.description: Chorus frogs calling from flooded ditches and vernal pools, sound like running a finger along a comb
12.childFriendlyNote: Run your thumbnail along a comb's teeth. That's what this tiny frog sounds like! Can you hear them at the puddle?

12.description: Hepatica blooming on woodland slopes, delicate pink, white, or lavender flowers emerging through leaf litter
12.childFriendlyNote: Tiny flowers in pink, white, or purple push up through the crunchy brown leaves on the forest floor, spring's first woodland treasure!

12.description: Robins singing "cheerily cheer-up cheerio" at dawn, males establishing nesting territories on lawns
12.childFriendlyNote: The robin sings "cheerily cheer-up cheerio!" from a treetop at sunrise. It's the alarm clock of spring!

12.description: Red-tailed hawks on nests, incubating eggs in large stick platforms high in trees
12.childFriendlyNote: The big hawk sits very still on her nest of sticks way up in a tall tree. She's keeping her eggs warm!

12.description: Sandhill crane migration tapering off, resident pairs beginning to establish nesting territories in marshes
12.childFriendlyNote: Some cranes keep flying north, but a few stay right here. They dance and bow to each other to say "this is our home!"

13.description: Bloodroot unfurling white petals around golden centers on woodland floors, each flower wrapped in a single lobed leaf
13.childFriendlyNote: A white flower opens like a tiny star, wrapped in its own leaf like a blanket. If you broke the stem (don't!) it would bleed orange!

13.description: Spring peeper chorus at full volume from every pond, vernal pool, and wet ditch
13.childFriendlyNote: The whole pond rings with peeping, hundreds of thumb-sized frogs singing their hearts out for love!

13.description: Eastern phoebes returned, pumping tails on fence posts and calling raspy "fee-bee" near bridges and barns
13.childFriendlyNote: A grey bird sits on a fence post bobbing its tail up and down and calling "fee-bee!", like it's saying its name!

13.description: Robins in full song at dawn and dusk, some pairs already building mud-cup nests in sheltered spots
13.childFriendlyNote: The robin carries a beak full of mud and grass to build a perfect round bowl for her eggs. She's an amazing builder!

13.description: Killdeer nesting on gravel rooftops and parking lots, performing broken-wing display if you approach
13.childFriendlyNote: If you walk near her eggs, the mama killdeer pretends her wing is broken to trick you into following her instead!

13.description: Red maples bursting with tiny red flowers, giving bare branches a rosy haze against grey skies
13.childFriendlyNote: The bare tree branches glow red with teeny tiny flowers. Squint your eyes and the whole tree looks like it's blushing!

14.description: Crab apple buds swelling and showing pink, earliest trees beginning to open in sheltered urban spots
14.childFriendlyNote: Pink buds are getting fat on the crab apple tree. They look like little round candies about to pop open!

14.description: Robins nesting in earnest, first blue eggs appearing in mud-and-grass cup nests
14.childFriendlyNote: The robin laid beautiful blue eggs! They're the color of the sky on a perfect spring day

14.description: Phoebes building mossy nests under eaves, bridges, and overhangs, tail-pumping from nearby perches
14.childFriendlyNote: The phoebe builds her nest under a bridge using mud and soft green moss. It looks like a little fuzzy shelf!

14.description: Virginia bluebells emerging in floodplain woods, pink buds opening to sky-blue trumpet-shaped flowers
14.childFriendlyNote: These flowers start as pink buds and turn blue when they open, like a magic color-changing trick!

14.description: Peeper chorus beginning to fade on warmest nights as breeding wraps up
14.childFriendlyNote: The peepers are getting quieter now. They've found their sweethearts and laid their eggs in the pond

14.description: Canada geese on nests near ponds and lakes, females incubating while ganders stand guard nearby
14.childFriendlyNote: The daddy goose stands guard while the mama sits on her nest. Don't get too close or he'll hiss at you!

15.description: Virginia bluebells carpeting floodplain forests in sheets of blue, peak bloom along streams
15.childFriendlyNote: The forest floor looks like someone spilled blue paint everywhere, thousands of blue bell-shaped flowers nodding in the breeze!

15.description: Crab apple trees bursting into bloom, clouds of pink and white blossoms humming with bees
15.childFriendlyNote: The crab apple tree exploded into pink flowers! Close your eyes and smell. It's like the sweetest perfume in the world

15.description: First yellow warblers arriving from Central America, bright yellow birds singing from willow thickets
15.childFriendlyNote: A tiny sunshine-yellow bird sings "sweet sweet sweet I'm so sweet!" from a bush. It just flew here from Mexico!

15.description: Redbud trees blooming with clusters of magenta-pink flowers directly on branches and trunk
15.childFriendlyNote: Pink flowers grow right out of the bark and branches. The whole tree looks like it's decorated for a party!

15.description: American toads trilling from shallow ponds, a long musical trill lasting 10-30 seconds
15.childFriendlyNote: A warty toad puffs up his throat like a balloon and makes a beautiful long trill. Who knew toads could sing so pretty?

15.description: Dandelions opening across lawns and fields, bright yellow flowers attracting early pollinators
15.childFriendlyNote: Golden dandelions pop open all over the grass like little suns. Bees love them because they're the first big meal of spring!

16.description: Lilac buds forming and swelling, leaves unfurling on bushes, fragrant bloom approaching
16.childFriendlyNote: The lilac bush is getting ready. Fat green buds are growing bigger every day, about to burst into the best-smelling flowers ever!

16.description: Dandelions in full bloom across every lawn and meadow, carpets of yellow
16.childFriendlyNote: Lawns have turned into golden fields of dandelions. Pick one and hold it under your chin to see if you like butter!

16.description: First barn swallows arriving, swooping low over fields and ponds catching insects on the wing
16.childFriendlyNote: Swoopy birds with forked tails zip just above the grass catching bugs in mid-air. They never miss!

16.description: Large-flowered trillium blooming in rich deciduous woods, three white petals above three green leaves
16.childFriendlyNote: Everything about this flower comes in threes: three white petals, three green leaves, three green sepals. Nature loves the number three!

16.description: Very first ruby-throated hummingbirds arriving from Gulf crossing, seeking nectar at early flowers and feeders
16.childFriendlyNote: A tiny bird that can fly backwards zips up to a flower! It's no bigger than your thumb and its wings buzz like a bee

16.description: Redbud at peak bloom, understory glowing pink in woodlands and along streets
16.childFriendlyNote: The redbud trees are glowing pink. Look under the big trees and you'll see these smaller trees shining like neon signs!

17.description: Lilac flower clusters beginning to open, first waves of fragrance drifting through neighborhoods
17.childFriendlyNote: The lilacs are starting to open! Bury your nose in a flower bunch and breathe deep. It smells like purple dreams

17.description: First Baltimore orioles arriving, brilliant orange-and-black males singing from treetops and visiting orange halves
17.childFriendlyNote: A bird as orange as a traffic cone sings a flute-like song from the tallest tree. Put out an orange half and he might visit!

17.description: Trillium at peak bloom, woodland floors dotted with large three-petaled white flowers
17.childFriendlyNote: The forest floor is decorated with big white three-petaled flowers. They'll turn pink as they get older, like blushing!

17.description: Ruby-throated hummingbirds arriving in numbers, males flashing iridescent red gorgets at feeders
17.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbird's throat flashes bright red when the sun hits it, like a tiny ruby necklace that appears and disappears!

17.description: Spring warbler migration building, mixed flocks of colorful warblers moving through treetops
17.childFriendlyNote: Tiny colorful birds flit through the treetops like living jewels, yellow ones, striped ones, spotted ones. They're passing through on a long journey!

17.description: Violets blooming in lawns, woodland edges, and along paths, purple, white, and bicolor forms
17.childFriendlyNote: Little purple violets hide in the grass like tiny faces peeking up at you. They're so small you might step on them if you're not careful!

18.description: Lilacs approaching peak bloom, heavy flower clusters perfuming entire streets and gardens
18.childFriendlyNote: Walk down any street and your nose fills with sweet lilac. Pick a tiny flower and you'll see it has four petals. Find one with five for good luck!

18.description: Orioles now common, females weaving intricate hanging nests from plant fibers in elm and cottonwood branches
18.childFriendlyNote: The mama oriole weaves a hanging basket-nest that swings in the wind. She's the best weaver in the bird world!

18.description: Peak warbler migration, treetops alive with dozens of species passing through, binoculars essential
18.childFriendlyNote: The trees are full of tiny bright birds today! This one has a throat as orange as a flame. It's called a Blackburnian warbler

18.description: Dandelions going to seed, white puffball heads ready to scatter in the wind
18.childFriendlyNote: Make a wish and blow! Each tiny parachute carries a seed to grow a new dandelion somewhere far away

18.description: Hummingbirds now regular at feeders and flowers, males performing U-shaped courtship dives
18.childFriendlyNote: The boy hummingbird flies way up high then swoops down in a big U-shape (wheeee!) to impress the girl hummingbird

18.description: Wild plum thickets covered in white blossoms, sweet fragrance attracting bees and butterflies along fencerows
18.childFriendlyNote: Bushes along fences are covered in white flowers that smell like honey. Bees are buzzing all around them like tiny helicopters!

19.description: Lilacs at peak bloom, the quintessential Midwest spring fragrance heavy in the air
19.childFriendlyNote: Lilac time! The big purple flower bunches are the best-smelling thing in the whole neighborhood. Take a biiiig sniff!

19.description: Orioles singing rich fluty songs from cottonwoods, visiting grape jelly and orange feeders
19.childFriendlyNote: Put out grape jelly on a plate and the bright orange oriole will come eat it. Birds love grape jelly just like you!

19.description: Indigo buntings arriving, impossibly blue males singing from power lines and hedgerow tops
19.childFriendlyNote: A bird as blue as a blueberry sits on a wire and sings. He looks like a piece of sky that learned to fly!

19.description: Milkweed shoots pushing up through soil in meadows and roadsides, thick fuzzy stems emerging
19.childFriendlyNote: Fat fuzzy green stalks push up from the ground. These plants are so important because monarch butterflies need them to survive!

19.description: Tiger swallowtail butterflies appearing, large yellow-and-black striped wings floating along garden paths
19.childFriendlyNote: A butterfly as big as your hand floats past. It's yellow with black tiger stripes and little blue spots near its tail!

19.description: Last waves of warbler migration passing through, mixed species flocks in woodland canopy
19.childFriendlyNote: A black-and-white striped bird creeps along a branch like a tiny zebra. It walks up and down tree trunks looking for bugs!

20.description: Lilac blooms fading, petals browning as the season's most iconic fragrance winds down
20.childFriendlyNote: The lilac flowers are turning brown and crinkly. Say goodbye until next spring, but remember that amazing smell!

20.description: Milkweed plants growing rapidly, large oval opposite leaves unfurling along sturdy stems
20.childFriendlyNote: The milkweed leaves are big and fuzzy like green velvet. Snap a leaf (carefully!) and white milky sap oozes out. That's how it got its name!

20.description: Indigo buntings now widespread, males singing persistently from exposed perches through the heat of the day
20.childFriendlyNote: The electric-blue bird sings all day long from the highest wire. Even when it's hot, he just keeps singing and singing!

20.description: Hummingbirds nesting, female building walnut-sized nest of lichen and spider silk on a branch
20.childFriendlyNote: The mama hummingbird builds the tiniest nest, smaller than a walnut! She glues it together with sticky spider webs

20.description: Very first fireflies blinking at dusk in moist meadows and woodland edges, season just beginning
20.childFriendlyNote: Just when the sky gets dark, tiny golden lights blink on and off in the grass. The fireflies are back! They make light with their bottoms!

21.description: Fireflies increasing nightly, males flying in J-shaped patterns with yellow-green flashes at dusk
21.childFriendlyNote: Watch closely. Each firefly flies up in a little J-shape and flashes! The girls in the grass flash back to say "I see you!"

21.description: Milkweed flower buds forming, round clusters visible at the top of tall stems
21.childFriendlyNote: The milkweed is getting ready to bloom. Round green buds at the top look like little broccoli bunches!

21.description: Barn swallows nesting under eaves and in barns, mud cup nests with feather linings
21.childFriendlyNote: The swallows built a mud nest right under the roof! They carry tiny balls of mud in their beaks, one trip at a time

21.description: Tiger swallowtails common at flowers and mud puddles, graceful gliding flight through gardens
21.childFriendlyNote: The big striped butterfly sips from puddles on the ground. Butterflies need minerals from mud, not just flower nectar!

21.description: Red clover blooming in meadows and roadsides, fuzzy pink-purple flower heads buzzing with bumblebees
21.childFriendlyNote: Pull out a tiny pink tube from the clover flower and suck the bottom. There's a teeny drop of sweet nectar inside!

22.description: Firefly displays intensifying, yards and meadows twinkling with hundreds of blinking lights after sunset
22.childFriendlyNote: The whole backyard is twinkling like a Christmas tree! Catch a firefly gently in your cupped hands and watch it glow through your fingers

22.description: Milkweed beginning to bloom, round clusters of pink-purple flowers opening, intensely sweet fragrance
22.childFriendlyNote: The milkweed flowers smell like grape candy! Each tiny flower is shaped like a little crown with a sweet surprise inside for butterflies

22.description: First monarch butterflies arriving from the south, seeking milkweed to lay eggs on
22.childFriendlyNote: The orange-and-black monarch butterfly flew here from far away. She's looking for milkweed because that's the only plant her babies can eat!

22.description: Orioles feeding nestlings in hanging basket nests, adults busy catching caterpillars
22.childFriendlyNote: The mama and papa oriole fly back and forth all day bringing caterpillars to hungry babies in their swinging basket nest!

22.description: Big bluestem grass growing rapidly in prairies and meadows, already knee-high with blue-green stems
22.childFriendlyNote: This prairie grass grows so tall: right now it's up to your knees, but by August it'll be taller than your dad!

23.description: Peak firefly season, synchronized flashing in some areas, magical displays over dewy meadows
23.childFriendlyNote: It looks like the ground is full of tiny stars floating up into the sky, the best light show on Earth and it's free!

23.description: Milkweed in full bloom, heavy round flower clusters attracting bees, butterflies, and beetles
23.childFriendlyNote: The milkweed flowers are like a busy airport, bees, butterflies, and beetles all landing and taking off at the same pink flower!

23.description: Monarch females laying eggs on milkweed undersides, tiny white eggs smaller than a pinhead
23.childFriendlyNote: Flip a milkweed leaf over gently. Can you find a tiny white egg? That egg will become a monarch caterpillar in just 4 days!

23.description: First black-eyed Susans opening in meadows and roadsides, cheerful yellow petals around dark brown centers
23.childFriendlyNote: Yellow flowers with brown button noses are popping up everywhere. They look like tiny sunflowers waving hello!

23.description: Bullfrogs calling from ponds with deep resonant "jug-o-rum" bass notes on warm evenings
23.childFriendlyNote: The biggest frog makes the deepest sound ("jug-o-rum!") like a bass drum at the pond. Can you make that sound?

23.description: Red clover in full bloom across meadows and playing fields, bumblebees working every flower head
23.childFriendlyNote: The clover field smells sweet and hums with bumblebees. Sit still and watch a fuzzy bee climb all over a pink flower ball!

24.description: Monarch caterpillars feeding on milkweed, black-yellow-white striped caterpillars munching leaves
24.childFriendlyNote: Striped caterpillars are chomping milkweed leaves. They eat and eat and eat until they're 2000 times heavier than when they hatched!

24.description: Firefly displays continuing strong on warm humid evenings, multiple species flashing different patterns
24.childFriendlyNote: Different kinds of fireflies flash different patterns: some blink fast, some slow, some make little swoops of light!

24.description: Milkweed flowers fading, green seed pods beginning to form where pollinated flowers were
24.childFriendlyNote: The milkweed flowers are done but bumpy green pods are growing where flowers used to be. Those pods are full of magic for later!

24.description: Black-eyed Susans spreading across roadsides and meadows, bright yellow daisies with brown domes
24.childFriendlyNote: Roadsides glow with yellow flowers. Each one has a fuzzy brown bump in the middle like a button nose!

24.description: Big bluestem now waist-high and growing fast, the iconic tall grass of the Midwest prairie
24.childFriendlyNote: The prairie grass is up to your waist now! Run your hand along the blue-green stems. They feel smooth and cool

24.description: Dragonflies patrolling over ponds and streams, males defending sunny perches, wings glinting in sunlight
24.childFriendlyNote: Dragonflies zip over the pond like tiny helicopters. They can fly forward, backward, and even hover in one spot!

25.description: Monarch caterpillars forming jade-green chrysalises with gold dots, transformation underway
25.childFriendlyNote: The caterpillar hangs upside down in a J-shape, then its skin splits and underneath is a beautiful green jewel box with real gold spots!

25.description: Firefly season beginning to wane, displays still visible but fewer individuals each night
25.childFriendlyNote: The firefly show is getting quieter. Enjoy each twinkling light because soon they'll disappear until next summer!

25.description: Black-eyed Susans at peak, fields and roadsides blazing with yellow blooms
25.childFriendlyNote: Fields of yellow flowers stretch as far as you can see. It looks like someone painted the whole meadow gold!

25.description: Purple coneflowers opening in prairies and gardens, droopy pink-purple petals around spiky orange cones
25.childFriendlyNote: This flower looks like it's having a bad hair day, pink petals drooping down around a spiky orange-brown pincushion. Bees love it!

25.description: Green darner dragonflies hawking insects over ponds and fields, large and brilliantly colored
25.childFriendlyNote: The biggest dragonfly has a bright green body and clear wings. It catches mosquitoes right out of the air. Thank you, dragonfly!

26.description: New generation of monarchs emerging from chrysalises, fresh orange wings drying in the sun
26.childFriendlyNote: The green jewel box cracks open and out crawls a wet, crumpled butterfly. In an hour its wings unfold and it flies away! Magic!

26.description: Big bluestem now shoulder-high, characteristic blue-green stems and reddish joints visible
26.childFriendlyNote: The prairie grass is taller than you now! Stand in it and you'll feel like an ant in a jungle

26.description: Coneflowers in full bloom, prairies and gardens dotted with pink-purple daisy-like blooms
26.childFriendlyNote: Touch the spiky center cone. It's prickly! Goldfinches will eat these seeds later, so leave the dried flowers standing

26.description: Bullfrogs calling loudly from every pond, bass "jug-o-rum" chorus on warm humid nights
26.childFriendlyNote: The pond is like a frog concert at night, deep "jug-o-rum" from the big bullfrogs and high peeps from the little ones!

26.description: Wild bergamot opening lavender pom-pom flowers in prairies and meadow edges, minty fragrance when touched
26.childFriendlyNote: Rub a leaf between your fingers and sniff. Surprise! It smells like mint! The purple pom-pom flowers are butterfly magnets

27.description: Second generation monarchs nectaring on milkweed and coneflowers, laying eggs for the next generation
27.childFriendlyNote: These monarchs were born here and now they're laying eggs for more babies: grandchildren of the butterflies that flew up from the south!

27.description: Coneflowers attracting fritillary butterflies and bumblebees, peak prairie wildflower season
27.childFriendlyNote: Orange butterflies called fritillaries crowd the pink coneflowers. It's like a butterfly party and everyone's invited!

27.description: Wild bergamot at peak bloom, lavender flowers alive with bumblebees, hummingbird moths, and butterflies
27.childFriendlyNote: A creature that looks like a tiny hummingbird is hovering at the flower. Surprise, it's actually a moth with clear wings!

27.description: Male goldfinches in brilliant lemon-yellow breeding plumage, bouncing flight over meadows with "po-ta-to-chip" call
27.childFriendlyNote: A bird as yellow as a lemon bounces through the air like it's on a roller coaster, calling "po-ta-to-chip!" with every bounce!

27.description: Big bluestem towering overhead, flower heads beginning to form, the "turkey foot" three-pronged seed heads appearing
27.childFriendlyNote: The grass is so tall you could hide in it! Look at the top. It splits into three parts that look like a turkey's foot!

28.description: Multiple monarch generations overlapping, caterpillars, chrysalises, and adults all present on milkweed patches
28.childFriendlyNote: Check one milkweed patch and you might find an egg, a caterpillar, a green chrysalis, and a flying butterfly, the whole life story in one spot!

28.description: Blazing star spikes opening from the top down, magenta-purple torches rising above the prairie grasses
28.childFriendlyNote: Tall purple torches poke up above the grass. They bloom from the top down, not the bottom up! How backwards is that?

28.description: Goldfinches beginning to nest, one of the latest nesting songbirds, timing nest-building to thistle and milkweed fluff availability
28.childFriendlyNote: The goldfinch waited until now to build a nest. She lines it with soft thistle fluff to make the coziest baby bed ever!

28.description: Dog-day cicadas beginning to buzz from treetops, their droning hum the soundtrack of Midwest summer
28.childFriendlyNote: That loud buzzing eeeeeee from the trees? That's a cicada! It spent years underground and now it's singing as loud as it can

28.description: Multiple dragonfly species over ponds, twelve-spotted skimmers perching on stems with boldly patterned wings
28.childFriendlyNote: This dragonfly has white and brown patches on its wings like a checkerboard. Count the spots! There should be twelve

29.description: Cicada chorus building to full volume on hot afternoons, buzzing from every mature tree
29.childFriendlyNote: The trees are buzzing so loud on hot days! Find a crunchy brown cicada shell stuck to a tree trunk. The bug left it behind like an empty spacesuit

29.description: Monarch population building, fresh butterflies nectaring on bergamot, coneflower, and milkweed
29.childFriendlyNote: More and more orange butterflies appear each week. They're multiplying! Soon a very special generation will be born...

29.description: Blazing star at peak bloom, magenta spires attracting monarchs and swallowtails in prairie remnants
29.childFriendlyNote: Purple flower torches light up the prairie and butterflies can't resist them. It's like a butterfly highway rest stop!

29.description: Black-eyed Susans still going strong, some beginning to form dark seed heads
29.childFriendlyNote: The yellow flowers are still smiling but some are losing their petals. The brown center is turning into a seed ball for birds to eat later

29.description: Bullfrog tadpoles visible in shallow pond edges, some from last year nearly ready to transform
29.childFriendlyNote: Big fat tadpoles with tiny back legs swim in the pond shallows. They're slowly turning into frogs! It takes a whole year

30.description: Peak dog-day cicada season, relentless buzzing from dawn to dusk on the hottest days
30.childFriendlyNote: The hotter it gets, the louder the cicadas buzz! They're like nature's thermometer: the noisier they are, the hotter it is

30.description: Late-summer monarch generation emerging, the generation that will undertake the great migration south
30.childFriendlyNote: Something special is happening. The monarchs born now won't lay eggs. Instead, they'll fly 2000 miles to Mexico! They're the super-generation!

30.description: Milkweed seed pods growing large and bumpy, green and warty on dried brown stalks
30.childFriendlyNote: Fat bumpy green pods hang from the milkweed. Don't open them yet! Inside, hundreds of seeds with fluffy parachutes are getting ready

30.description: Goldenrod flower buds forming, tall yellow-green stems beginning to show gold at the tips
30.childFriendlyNote: Tall green stalks are starting to turn gold at the top. Soon the whole meadow will glow like treasure!

30.description: Big bluestem at full height, 6-8 feet tall with purple-bronze turkey-foot seed heads waving above the prairie
30.childFriendlyNote: The prairie grass towers over everyone's head! Walk through it and listen. The wind makes it whisper and rustle like the ocean

31.description: Goldenrod bursting into bloom, meadows and roadsides turning gold with arching flower plumes
31.childFriendlyNote: Fields are turning gold! Goldenrod is not what makes you sneeze (that's ragweed). Goldenrod is the bees' favorite late-summer feast

31.description: Monarchs nectaring heavily on goldenrod and asters, fueling up for their long migration south
31.childFriendlyNote: The monarchs are eating and eating. They need to store lots of energy in their bodies for the longest trip any butterfly ever takes!

31.description: Cicadas still droning in late July heat, empty nymph shells accumulating on tree trunks
31.childFriendlyNote: Collect the see-through cicada shells off tree trunks. They're perfect tiny hollow copies of the bug, even the legs! Totally harmless to touch

31.description: Milkweed pods maturing, some beginning to dry and split, revealing tightly packed silk-tufted seeds
31.childFriendlyNote: Crack open a ripe milkweed pod. Inside are rows of flat brown seeds each with a fluffy white parachute, packed tight like sardines!

31.description: Green darner dragonflies still hunting over ponds, late-season emergence overlapping with early migrants
31.childFriendlyNote: The big green dragonfly zooms back and forth over the pond. It eats hundreds of mosquitoes every single day. What a hero!

32.description: Goldenrod at peak bloom, entire meadows glowing gold, alive with bees, wasps, and soldier beetles
32.childFriendlyNote: The goldenrod meadow is humming with hundreds of bees. Stand still and listen to the buzzing all around you!

32.description: New England asters beginning to bloom, deep purple daisy-like flowers joining goldenrod in meadows
32.childFriendlyNote: Purple flowers are joining the gold ones. Together they make the meadow look like a purple-and-gold painting!

32.description: Monarchs beginning to drift southward, clusters sometimes visible at roost sites in evenings
32.childFriendlyNote: The monarchs are starting their incredible journey south! At night they gather in trees together, sometimes 50 butterflies on one branch!

32.description: Cicada chorus beginning to thin as summer wanes, still loud on the hottest afternoons
32.childFriendlyNote: The cicadas are getting a little quieter. Summer is starting to slip away but the buzz is still there on hot afternoons

32.description: Sumac fruit clusters ripening to deep red, fuzzy cone-shaped berry clusters at branch tips
32.childFriendlyNote: Red fuzzy berry clusters stand up like torches at the end of branches. They feel like velvet and birds will eat them all winter!

33.description: Goldenrod still in full bloom, some early flowers beginning to set fluffy seeds
33.childFriendlyNote: Goldenrod gall flies lay eggs inside the stems. Look for round swollen bumps on the stalks. There's a tiny grub living inside!

33.description: Asters spreading along roadsides and meadow edges, purple flowers with yellow centers opening daily
33.childFriendlyNote: Dozens of purple daisies with bright yellow eyes open up along the path. They only open in the sunshine!

33.description: Monarch migration intensifying, butterflies streaming south through meadows, following goldenrod corridors
33.childFriendlyNote: Orange butterflies float past heading south. Each one is on a 2000-mile journey to a mountain forest in Mexico they've never been to!

33.description: Common nighthawks gathering in flocks for southward migration, swooping over parking lots and fields at dusk
33.childFriendlyNote: At sunset, birds with pointy wings swoop and dive over the parking lot eating bugs. They look like little jet fighters with white wing stripes!

33.description: Green darner dragonflies beginning their own migration south, flying in loose groups on north winds
33.childFriendlyNote: Did you know dragonflies migrate too? Green darners fly south just like monarchs. Look for groups of them heading the same direction!

34.description: Peak monarch migration through the Midwest, hundreds visible on a good day in meadows and gardens
34.childFriendlyNote: It's the biggest monarch wave! Look at the sky. Orange butterflies drift south like floating autumn leaves. Wave goodbye and wish them luck!

34.description: Goldenrod flowers turning to fluffy seeds, still attracting late-season pollinators
34.childFriendlyNote: The goldenrod is going fuzzy. Gold flowers are turning into tiny cotton-puff seeds that blow away in the wind

34.description: Asters at peak bloom, taking over from goldenrod as the last big flower show of the season
34.childFriendlyNote: While goldenrod fades, the purple asters take over, autumn's last purple hurrah before the flowers go to sleep!

34.description: Sandhill cranes beginning to gather in pre-migration staging areas, family groups visible in agricultural fields
34.childFriendlyNote: Tall grey cranes with red caps are gathering in big groups in farm fields. They're planning their trip south together!

34.description: Sumac leaves beginning to turn brilliant scarlet, one of the first trees to show fall color
34.childFriendlyNote: Sumac is always first to turn red in fall, bright scarlet leaves glowing at the edge of fields like nature's stop signs!

35.description: Monarch migration continuing, butterflies funneling south through the region on favorable winds
35.childFriendlyNote: The monarch parade continues. Each butterfly weighs less than a paperclip but flies all the way to Mexico!

35.description: Asters still blooming strong, providing crucial late-season nectar for migrating butterflies and bees
35.childFriendlyNote: Purple asters are the last flower diner of the season. Bumblebees stuff themselves silly before the cold comes!

35.description: Big bluestem turning bronze and copper, turkey-foot seed heads ripe and scattering in the wind
35.childFriendlyNote: The tall prairie grass has turned copper and bronze. It rustles and whispers when the wind blows through like a secret prairie song

35.description: Large flocks of nighthawks migrating south, dozens visible swooping over cities and fields at dusk
35.childFriendlyNote: Look up at sunset. Pointy-winged nighthawks swoop in big groups over the buildings, catching bugs as they fly south!

35.description: Sumac in full scarlet, flaming red leaves standing out dramatically against still-green surroundings
35.childFriendlyNote: The sumac looks like it's on fire. Bright red leaves glow against all the still-green trees. It's fall's first firework!

36.description: Sandhill cranes gathering in large staging flocks, hundreds in cornfields and wet meadows preparing to migrate
36.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of cranes fill the cornfields, making a rattling bugle sound you can hear a mile away. It's crane school for migration!

36.description: Asters at full peak along every roadside and meadow edge, the last great wildflower display
36.childFriendlyNote: Purple asters line every path like nature planted a flower garden just for the end of summer!

36.description: Milkweed pods splitting open, silk-parachuted seeds floating on autumn breezes
36.childFriendlyNote: Milkweed pods crack open and hundreds of silky seeds float away on tiny parachutes. Catch one and make a wish!

36.description: Hummingbirds migrating south, visiting feeders and late flowers intensely to fuel their Gulf crossing
36.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbirds are leaving! They eat extra nectar to get fat enough to fly 500 miles across the ocean without stopping!

36.description: First white-throated sparrows arriving from the north, scratching in leaf litter and singing sweet "Oh Sam Peabody" songs
36.childFriendlyNote: A new bird arrives singing "Oh sweet Canada Canada Canada". It spent the summer up north and comes here for winter like a snowbird!

37.description: Crane staging reaching peak numbers, massive flocks lifting off at dawn and returning at dusk to roost
37.childFriendlyNote: At sunrise, the cranes all lift off at once. Thousands of grey wings and bugling calls fill the sky! It sounds like a dinosaur stampede!

37.description: Sugar maples beginning to turn color, first gold and orange appearing in canopy tops
37.childFriendlyNote: Look at the tippy-top of the maple tree. The leaves are turning gold and orange! Fall color starts at the top and works its way down

37.description: White-throated sparrows now common in brushy edges, sweet whistled song a signature autumn sound
37.childFriendlyNote: Listen for a sweet whistle ("Oh sweet Canada Canada Canada!") from the bushes. This sparrow has a bright white throat like a little bib!

37.description: Woolly bear caterpillars crossing paths and roads, fuzzy black-and-rust banded caterpillars seeking hibernation spots
37.childFriendlyNote: A fuzzy black-and-brown caterpillar crosses the sidewalk. Pick it up gently and it curls into a ball! Legend says a wider brown band means a mild winter

37.description: Asters beginning to fade, some still blooming but many going to fluffy seed
37.childFriendlyNote: The purple asters are getting fluffy and grey. Their petals fall off and tiny seeds with cotton-puff parachutes take their place

38.description: Sugar maple fall color intensifying, brilliant orange-gold-red transforming canopies in woodlands and streets
38.childFriendlyNote: The sugar maples are on fire with color! Orange, gold, and red all on the same tree. It looks like a sunset grew leaves

38.description: Crane flocks beginning to depart southward, long V-formations and spiraling kettles visible on clear days
38.childFriendlyNote: The cranes are leaving! Long lines of big grey birds fly south, calling back and forth so nobody gets lost

38.description: Woolly bears commonly seen crossing sidewalks and roads, urgently seeking shelter before frost
38.childFriendlyNote: Woolly bears are everywhere, crossing sidewalks on a mission. They need to find a hiding spot before winter. Help one cross safely!

38.description: Red oaks starting to turn, leaves shifting from green to russet-brown and deep burgundy
38.childFriendlyNote: Oak leaves are turning reddish-brown. Collect the best ones and the big round acorns underneath. Squirrels are doing the same thing!

38.description: White-throated sparrows now abundant, mixed flocks shuffling through leaf litter in woods and gardens
38.childFriendlyNote: Sparrows kick through the fallen leaves with both feet at once, scratch-scratch-scratch, looking for hidden seeds and bugs!

39.description: Sugar maples at peak fall color, entire hillsides ablaze in orange, gold, and scarlet
39.childFriendlyNote: This is it, peak fall color! Every tree is showing off its best outfit. Catch a falling leaf and it's good luck!

39.description: Red oaks deepening to rich burgundy and russet, acorns dropping and rolling underfoot
39.childFriendlyNote: Acorns plonk down from the big oak trees. Each one has a little hat! Squirrels are scrambling to grab them before anyone else

39.description: Squirrels frantically caching acorns, walnuts, and hickory nuts, burying hundreds for winter retrieval
39.childFriendlyNote: Watch the squirrel dig a little hole, drop in an acorn, pat the dirt down, and zip off for another. She'll bury 10,000 nuts this fall!

39.description: Cottonwoods turning bright golden yellow, massive trees glowing along rivers and streams
39.childFriendlyNote: Giant cottonwood trees along the river turn pure gold. Their leaves shimmer and rattle in the wind like golden coins!

39.description: Last woolly bears still crossing paths, curling into tight fuzzy balls when disturbed
39.childFriendlyNote: This fuzzy caterpillar will survive being frozen solid this winter! It makes its own antifreeze and wakes up in spring. Incredible!

40.description: Sugar maple leaves falling in golden-orange showers, carpeting ground beneath trees
40.childFriendlyNote: Walk through the crunchy carpet of fallen leaves. Crunch crunch crunch! Scoop up a pile and throw them in the air!

40.description: White-throated sparrows abundant in brushy areas, their whistled song a constant autumn soundtrack
40.childFriendlyNote: The sweet "Oh Canada Canada Canada" whistle follows you everywhere in autumn. These little sparrows are winter friends!

40.description: Squirrels still caching nuts at a furious pace, also building leaf nests (dreys) high in trees for winter
40.childFriendlyNote: Look for big messy leaf balls up in the bare branches. Those are squirrel houses! They stuff them with leaves to stay warm all winter

40.description: Crab apple trees heavy with small red and yellow fruit, attracting robins, waxwings, and other fruit-eaters
40.childFriendlyNote: Tiny red apples hang on the tree like ornaments. Birds gobble them up! They're too sour for people but perfect for robins

40.description: Dark-eyed juncos returning from northern breeding grounds, first flocks appearing at feeders and woodland edges
40.childFriendlyNote: The little grey "snowbirds" are back! When you see juncos arrive, you know winter isn't far behind

41.description: Red oaks at peak russet-brown color, heavy leaf fall underway, acorns on the ground
41.childFriendlyNote: The oak leaves are falling like brown rain! Shuffle through the crunchy piles and listen to the rustling sound

41.description: White-throated sparrows now settled into winter territories, feeding flocks in leaf litter and under bushes
41.childFriendlyNote: Little sparrows with white-striped heads kick through the leaves together. They'll be your backyard friends all winter long!

41.description: Squirrels still burying last nuts, thick winter coats growing in, tails extra bushy
41.childFriendlyNote: The squirrels look extra fluffy now. Their fur is growing thicker for winter like putting on a puffy coat!

41.description: Juncos now regular at feeders and in flocks on the ground, grey and white winter visitors established
41.childFriendlyNote: Snowbirds everywhere! Juncos hop on the ground under the feeder, flashing white tail feathers when they fly up

41.description: Bittersweet vine capsules splitting open to reveal bright orange-red berries against bare branches
41.childFriendlyNote: Yellow shells pop open on a twisting vine to show bright orange-red berries inside, like nature's own surprise gift wrap!

42.description: Deer rut beginning, bucks with polished antlers making scrapes on ground and rubs on small trees
42.childFriendlyNote: The boy deer have big antlers now and rub them on trees. Look for shredded bark on small trees, that's where a buck was!

42.description: Junco flocks well established at feeders, sparring and chasing to determine winter flock hierarchy
42.childFriendlyNote: The juncos have little arguments at the feeder: peck, chase, flutter! They're deciding who's boss of the flock

42.description: Sugar maples nearly bare, last leaves rattling and falling, bare branch silhouettes emerging
42.childFriendlyNote: The maple trees are almost naked now! You can see the beautiful shapes of their branches that were hidden all summer

42.description: Starling flocks growing larger, beginning to form swirling murmurations at dusk over urban roost sites
42.childFriendlyNote: Thousands of birds swoop and swirl together at sunset like a giant living cloud. They twist and turn but never crash into each other!

42.description: Witch-hazel blooming with spidery yellow flowers on nearly bare branches, one of the last plants to bloom
42.childFriendlyNote: When every other flower has gone to sleep, witch-hazel blooms! Tiny yellow ribbons of petals open on bare branches, autumn's last surprise

43.description: Starling murmurations at peak, massive swirling flocks of thousands creating spectacular aerial displays
43.childFriendlyNote: Watch the sky at sunset. A cloud of birds flows and morphs like a magical shape-shifting creature! It's called a murmuration

43.description: Deer rut intensifying, bucks chasing does, increased deer movement and roadside sightings
43.childFriendlyNote: The deer are extra active now, running through fields and across roads. Be extra careful in the car! The boy deer are chasing the girls

43.description: Cardinals bright against grey bare trees, visiting feeders with increasing regularity as natural food diminishes
43.childFriendlyNote: The red cardinal glows against the grey bare branches like a little red light, so easy to spot now that the leaves are gone!

43.description: Juncos in settled winter flocks, common ground-feeders beneath bird feeders and along woodland edges
43.childFriendlyNote: Look under the bird feeder. A flock of grey juncos hops around eating all the seeds the bigger birds dropped!

43.description: Red-tailed hawks conspicuous on bare-branched perches along highways and field edges, hunting rodents
43.childFriendlyNote: With the leaves gone, you can finally see the big hawk sitting on a bare tree branch. Its red tail catches the sun!

44.description: Starling murmurations continuing, thousands roosting together in city trees and under bridges
44.childFriendlyNote: The starling cloud dances across the sunset sky. Expanding, shrinking, flowing like a river of birds. How do they not bump?

44.description: Peak of deer rut, bucks traveling widely, grunt-snort-wheeze calls audible in quiet woods
44.childFriendlyNote: The boy deer grunt and snort through the quiet autumn woods. They barely eat or sleep because they're so busy looking for a girlfriend!

44.description: Chickadees in winter flocks with nuthatches and downy woodpeckers, moving through leafless woods
44.childFriendlyNote: Chickadees team up with nuthatches and woodpeckers. They travel through the woods together like a little bird gang keeping watch for hawks!

44.description: Cardinals at feeders in pairs, females olive-green with orange bill, males brilliant red
44.childFriendlyNote: The lady cardinal isn't red. She's soft brown with orange touches. Can you spot her next to the bright red boy?

44.description: Red-tails perched prominently along highways, easily spotted in bare trees, screaming their raspy "keeeer"
44.childFriendlyNote: Drive along the highway and count the hawks on bare trees. That screaming "keeeeer!" sound in movies? That's actually this hawk!

45.description: Cardinals bright at feeders against grey November skies, short sharp chip calls from hedgerows
45.childFriendlyNote: On a grey November day, the red cardinal at the feeder is like a bright red fire truck in a parking lot, impossible to miss!

45.description: Junco flocks well settled for winter, hopping on frozen ground and under feeders
45.childFriendlyNote: The snowbirds hop around on the cold ground looking for seeds. They fluff up their feathers like little grey puffballs to stay warm

45.description: Chickadees adding extra alarm dee-notes when predators are near. More "dees" means greater danger
45.childFriendlyNote: Listen carefully. "chicka-dee-dee" means "I'm a little nervous." "chicka-dee-dee-dee-dee-dee" means "Danger! Hawk nearby!" More dees = more scared!

45.description: Red-tailed hawks perched along roads and on utility poles, easily visible against leafless landscape
45.childFriendlyNote: How many hawks can you count on a car ride? They sit on poles and bare trees looking for mice. See who spots the most!

45.description: Starlings in winter plumage covered in white speckles, large noisy flocks at roost sites
45.childFriendlyNote: Look closely at a starling. It's not plain black! In winter it's covered in tiny white dots like someone sprinkled it with stars

46.description: Late rut activity, bucks exhausted but still pursuing does, increased twilight and night movement
46.childFriendlyNote: The boy deer look tired now. They've been running around for weeks without eating much. Time to rest and get ready for winter!

46.description: Cardinals visiting feeders at first and last light, bright splash of color in bare November landscape
46.childFriendlyNote: The cardinal is the first bird at the feeder in the grey morning and the last one before dark, bookends of the day!

46.description: Chickadees roosting in tree cavities at night, each bird finding its own tiny shelter to survive cold nights
46.childFriendlyNote: At bedtime, each chickadee squeezes into a tiny tree hole all by itself and puffs up into a feathery ball to stay warm, like a sleeping bag made of feathers!

46.description: Starling murmurations still spectacular at dusk, birds streaming to urban roost sites from all directions
46.childFriendlyNote: From every direction, rivers of starlings pour toward the city at sunset. They all want to sleep in the same trees! Safety in numbers

46.description: Nuthatches wedging seeds into bark crevices and hammering them open, their "yank yank" calls ringing through bare woods
46.childFriendlyNote: The nuthatch jams a seed into a crack in the bark and whacks it open. It uses the tree like a nutcracker! Clever bird!

47.description: Juncos on frozen ground and at feeders, often the most numerous bird at Midwest winter feeding stations
47.childFriendlyNote: Count the juncos under your feeder. There might be twenty! They're dark on top and white underneath, like little grey-and-white cookies

47.description: Cardinals in winter feeding flocks, sometimes a dozen together at well-stocked feeders
47.childFriendlyNote: A whole flock of cardinals at the feeder! Red boys and brown girls. They look like decorations on a winter holiday tree

47.description: Red-tails hunting over stubble fields and along roadsides, soaring low on cloudy November days
47.childFriendlyNote: The hawk glides low over the bare cornfield. Its eyes are so sharp it can spot a mouse running from way up high!

47.description: Chickadee winter flocks working through bare trees, acrobatic feeding on hidden insect eggs and larvae
47.childFriendlyNote: The chickadee hangs upside down from a twig to find tiny bug eggs hiding in the bark. It's like a little circus acrobat!

47.description: Deer rut ending, bucks beginning to shed antlers, deer shifting to winter browse of twigs and bark
47.childFriendlyNote: The deer are dropping their antlers! If you find one on the ground, it's like finding buried treasure, a perfect souvenir from nature

48.description: Cardinals steady at feeders, bright color against first significant snowfalls of the season
48.childFriendlyNote: Red bird on white snow. The cardinal looks like a valentine against the first big snowfall! Pop, pop, cracking sunflower seeds

48.description: Chickadees visiting feeders frequently as temperatures drop, lowering body temperature at night to conserve energy
48.childFriendlyNote: The chickadee has a superpower. At night it gets colder on purpose to save energy! It's like turning down the thermostat inside its own body

48.description: Juncos on snowy ground, hopping and scratching to find seeds beneath fresh snow cover
48.childFriendlyNote: The snowbirds look right at home hopping on the white snow. Their dark backs and white bellies are perfect camouflage!

48.description: Nuthatches visiting suet feeders and creeping down bare tree trunks, retrieving cached seeds from bark
48.childFriendlyNote: Remember all those seeds the nuthatch hid in bark cracks last fall? Now it goes back to find them. It remembers where each one is!

48.description: Fox tracks appearing in first snow, thick winter coat making foxes look larger, mousing in snowy fields
48.childFriendlyNote: A fox pounces headfirst into the snow (boing!) to catch a mouse it heard under the white blanket. It looks so silly!

49.description: Cardinals singing occasional winter songs on milder mornings, brightening grey December days
49.childFriendlyNote: Even in cold December, the cardinal sings a few notes on warmer mornings, a tiny promise that spring will come back someday!

49.description: Barred owls beginning early courtship calling, "Who cooks for you?" echoing through snowy woods at dusk
49.childFriendlyNote: Shh. Listen in the cold dark woods! The owl is starting to call "Who cooks for you?" Owl love stories start in winter!

49.description: Chickadees in mixed-species winter flocks, the bold scout birds that investigate anything new
49.childFriendlyNote: Stand still in the snowy woods and the chickadees come to you. They're so curious, they'll land on your hat if you're patient!

49.description: Juncos dependable at feeders throughout December, twittering soft calls in ground-feeding flocks
49.childFriendlyNote: The juncos twitter softly as they hop around together, like they're whispering little winter secrets to each other!

49.description: Deer in winter mode, thick grey-brown coats, browsing on twigs and dried leaves in woodland cover
49.childFriendlyNote: The deer have fluffy grey winter coats now. Each hair is hollow and filled with air to trap warmth, like a built-in puffy jacket!

50.description: Cardinals glowing red at feeders against snow-covered landscape, regular dawn visitors
50.childFriendlyNote: A bright red bird on a snowy branch. It's like nature painted a picture just for December! The cardinal never migrates, it stays with you all year

50.description: Chickadees fluffed up against December cold, visiting feeders in quick dashes from sheltering evergreens
50.childFriendlyNote: The chickadee fluffs up so round in the cold it looks like a tiny feathered tennis ball with a beak. Grab a seed and zoom back to the tree!

50.description: Red-tails perched along roads, puffed against cold, scanning snowy fields for movement below
50.childFriendlyNote: The big hawk sits all fluffed up on a pole in the cold, patient as a statue, waiting and watching with its amazing hawk eyes

50.description: Downy woodpeckers tapping on bare branches and visiting suet feeders, bright red patch on male's nape
50.childFriendlyNote: The tiny woodpecker pecks at a block of suet (beef fat). Yum! It needs lots of energy to stay warm on freezing nights

50.description: Rabbits in winter brown pelage, tracks visible after snowfall, sheltering under brush piles
50.childFriendlyNote: After it snows, check the yard for bunny tracks. Two big back feet prints always land ahead of the two smaller front ones!

51.description: Cardinals dependable at feeders through the shortest days, first at the feeder at dawn, last at dusk
51.childFriendlyNote: The shortest day of the year is this week! But the cardinal still shows up faithfully. It never takes a day off from being beautiful

51.description: Great horned owls beginning courtship hooting, deep resonant "hoo-hoo-hoooo hoo-hoo" duets in the dark
51.childFriendlyNote: On a quiet winter night, two deep voices hoot back and forth: "hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo!" The biggest owls start their love songs in December!

51.description: Juncos at every feeder and along every woodland edge, the quintessential Midwest winter bird
51.childFriendlyNote: Juncos are everywhere in winter. Count how many you see today! They hop-hop-hop on the cold ground looking for any tiny seed

51.description: Chickadees greeting short winter days with cheerful calls, retrieving seeds cached months ago from bark crevices
51.childFriendlyNote: The chickadee remembers where it hid thousands of seeds! Each one tucked into a different crack in the bark months ago, what an amazing memory!

51.description: Foxes in beautiful thick winter fur, occasionally visible trotting across snowy fields at dawn or dusk
51.childFriendlyNote: If you're lucky, you might see a fox trotting across the snow. Its thick red fur looks so warm and its bushy tail trails behind like a flag!

52.description: Cardinals at winter feeders, their red plumage the brightest color in the holiday landscape
52.childFriendlyNote: The red cardinal on a snowy pine branch looks just like a Christmas card: nature's own holiday decoration, singing in the cold!

52.description: Chickadees brave and busy at feeders despite deep cold, flitting in groups through bare trees
52.childFriendlyNote: The cheerful chickadee doesn't care how cold it gets, "chicka-dee-dee-dee!" it says, as if to tell winter "You don't scare me!"

52.description: Great horned owl pairs duetting at dusk, deep hooting marking territory ahead of January nesting
52.childFriendlyNote: Step outside on a quiet cold night and listen. The deep "hoo hoo hoo hoo" of the great horned owl echoes through the winter darkness

52.description: Nuthatches at suet feeders and on tree trunks, nasal "yank yank" calls a familiar winter woodland sound
52.childFriendlyNote: The nuthatch walks headfirst down the tree again. It sees bugs hiding in bark that other birds miss because they only walk up!

52.description: Rabbit tracks in snow connecting brush piles and garden edges, nibbled bark visible on young trees
52.childFriendlyNote: Follow the bunny tracks in the snow from one bush to another. You can read the rabbit's whole morning adventure written in footprints!
